doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recording You Won't Forget Me with Toots, Wynton and Branford
summary: Toots did one take, Branford and Wynton two, and a party; Miles arrived early.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: But I wanted to just talk to you specifically about the You Won’t Forget Me album.

And those books that you recorded on, I know it was a homecoming of sorts, I guess, for Miles, certainly, and for Toots Tillman, for that book, early on in your career, and Winton and Branford were here as well. Can you discuss that experience, and the musicianship of what each of these gentlemen brought to that, their musicianship, and what each of these brought to this project?

Well, it was simple. And it was funny. I mean, it really got funny. Toots came in. We did one take, that was it. We had allotted four hours for everybody, right, and Branford came in; we did two takes. Wynton, we did two takes. Then we had a party Then the food came and we had fun, child, laughing and talking and everything. No, I‘m wrong. Yeah, we had a party, and then there was time in between. Well, Miles had to have a limo to bring him down one block, a stretch, and we didn‘t want Branford, I mean Wynton there when Miles came. They‘d be trying to get the guys out, those two especially. Okay, Miles came early. I said, ―Oh shit.‖ Wynton had just gone out the door, and it was funny. The engineer, everybody was in on it. We was laughing. It was really funny. And everybody was scared to death they would . . . but Richard had said, ―Don‘t anybody say anything to Miles. Don‘t anybody say it.‖
